{
  "B_expression": "-1/(2*(1+u)*((1+u)+sqrt((1+u)**2+r))**2)",
  "C_expression": "-1/(2*(1+u))",
  "derivation": "Retain the inherited exact-root coefficient pair. Set a=1+u and s=sqrt(a^2+r), the positive root. Inside the chi-supported core, p=z^2+r=a^2+r and the exact successor amplitude is s, so g=s-a=r/(a+s). The host form is g=r/2+r^2*B+u*r*C. Because a-u=1, the identity r/(a+s)=r/2-u*r/(2a)-r^2/(2a*(a+s)^2) holds, which is produced by C=-1/(2a) and B=-1/(2a*(a+s)^2). Thus (z+g)^2-p vanishes algebraically in the inner support, not merely the pure quadratic remainder; the cross term 2*u*g is included in the whole residual. The chi factors are fixed and C-infinity, so the correction is smoothly switched on and off. On the closed outer rectangle, a lies in [3/4,5/4] and a^2+r >= 1/16, so both bodies are smooth on an open neighborhood of the required domain. This is a source-relative local coefficient certificate only, not a full Navier-Stokes proof.",
  "inspect": [],
  "note": "Successor should retain this program for in-support stages. The state dependence through u is essential: the C term cancels the 2*u*g contribution in the whole residual when u is nonzero. Outside the chi support, or outside the outer rectangle, the complete program uses the linear r/2 fallback by design, so large-deviation rows with nonzero residual are not failures of this local construction. For future checks, verify only the local positivity conditions 1+u>0 and (1+u)^2+r>0 on a neighborhood of the closed outer rectangle. Do not treat the finite numerical residuals or the interval certificate as a global PDE certificate."
}
